name: Masala Chai
cuisine: Indian (pan-Indian tea-stall drink; Mumbai "cutting chai" culture)

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger (adrak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ inch piece, or ½ tsp grated

equipment: Small saucepan (about 500 ml): holds the chai with room for it to rise
Tea strainer (chai chhalni): to catch leaves and ginger
Mortar and pestle (khalbatta): to crush ginger and cardamom
Cup, spoon, measuring spoons, small ladle (optional, for "pulling" the chai)

steps.title: Measure the water and milk
steps.text: Measure 80 ml water and 100 ml full-fat milk into two separate cups.
steps.visualCue: Two small cups, the water just under the milk level
steps.cameraCheck: The two cups side by side
steps.videoShot: Pouring milk and water into two cups.
steps.watchOut: Eyeballing a full cup; the chai turns thin and weak (too much water) or too heavy (too much milk). Use a measuring cup or mark ⅓ and ½ cup in a steel cup.

steps.title: Crush the ginger and cardamom
steps.text: Peel 3 g ginger (½ inch), then crush it with 1 cardamom pod in a mortar until the ginger is coarsely broken and the pod has split.
steps.visualCue: Ginger in rough, damp pieces and the cardamom pod split open with black seeds showing; a sharp, sweet smell rises
steps.cameraCheck: The crushed ginger and cardamom in the mortar
steps.videoShot: A pestle pounding ginger and cardamom.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the ginger in a whole slice, so it gives little flavour; crush or grate it fine. If the cardamom smells flat, it is old; use a second pod.

steps.title: Boil the water with the spices
steps.text: Pour the 80 ml water into a small saucepan, add the crushed ginger and cardamom, and set it on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles form at the edge, then the water rolls with a steady boil and turns pale yellow, smelling of ginger
steps.cameraCheck: The saucepan with the water boiling and the spices in it
steps.videoShot: Water starting to boil with ginger pieces bobbing.
steps.watchOut: Walking away so most of the water boils off; stay at the stove, and if the pan is nearly dry, add 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Add the tea leaves
steps.text: Add 1 tsp (2 g) tea leaves to the boiling water and let it boil for 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: The water turns deep orange-brown within a few seconds, and the leaves unfurl and swirl
steps.cameraCheck: The tea leaves in a spoon before they go in, then the dark brown liquid
steps.videoShot: Tea granules dropping into boiling water and the colour blooming.
steps.watchOut: Boiling the leaves for 2-3 minutes, which makes the chai bitter and dark with a dry taste; keep to about 30 seconds and move straight on to the milk.

steps.title: Add the sugar
steps.visualCue: The crystals vanish within a few seconds and the liquid looks glossy
steps.cameraCheck: The spoon of sugar over the pan
steps.videoShot: Sugar being tipped into the dark tea.
steps.watchOut: Adding more sugar than planned out of habit, which is the main source of calories here; stick to 1½ tsp and taste at the end.

steps.title: Pour in the milk
steps.text: Pour in the 100 ml milk and stir once.
steps.visualCue: The liquid turns from dark brown to a light, creamy caramel brown
steps.cameraCheck: The pan showing the creamy light-brown colour
steps.videoShot: Milk swirling into the dark tea.
steps.watchOut: Cold milk added with the heat too high, which can make it rise suddenly; keep the heat at medium.

steps.title: Bring it to a boil
steps.text: Heat on medium, watching closely, until the chai foams up to nearly the rim of the pan.
steps.tip: Stay with the pan and keep a spoon ready; the rise takes only a second or two once it starts.
steps.visualCue: A thick tan foam climbs the sides of the pan, with a roasted, spicy smell
steps.cameraCheck: The foam just below the rim of the pan
steps.videoShot: Foam rising up the pan and the pan being lifted off the heat.
steps.watchOut: Boil-over, the most common chai mishap; the instant foam reaches the rim, lift the pan off the heat for 5 seconds, then put it back. If it spills, wipe the stove at once before the milk burns.

steps.title: Simmer briefly
steps.text: Let it simmer 30-60 seconds on low heat, then turn off the flame.
steps.visualCue: The foam settles and the colour deepens to a rich golden-brown, with the ginger smell now stronger
steps.cameraCheck: The finished chai in the pan, colour visible
steps.videoShot: Chai simmering gently and the flame turning off.
steps.watchOut: Simmering for several minutes, which gives a cooked, burnt-milk taste and a thick skin; stop at 1 minute. If you like it stronger, add a pinch more leaves at step 4 next time rather than boiling longer.

steps.title: Cover and rest
steps.text: Put a lid or plate on the pan and leave it for 1 minute.
steps.visualCue: The colour deepens a little more and steam drips on the lid
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan with a timer at 1 min
steps.videoShot: A lid being placed on the pan.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the rest, which gives a flatter flavour; the covered minute lets the spice and tea settle in. Do not leave it longer than 2 minutes, or it goes bitter.

steps.title: Strain and serve
steps.text: Pour the chai through a strainer into a cup.
steps.visualCue: A clear, glossy golden-brown liquid with a thin film of foam on top and ginger and leaves left in the strainer
steps.cameraCheck: The finished cup next to the strainer holding the leaves
steps.videoShot: Chai pouring in a stream through the strainer into a cup.
steps.watchOut: Pouring too fast so leaves slip through or hot chai splashes; pour in a slow, steady stream with the cup close to the pan.

reasons: no oil, no frying and very little salt; the milk gives calcium (about 12% of the day), riboflavin and B12, and ginger and cardamom add flavour without calories. Points off for added sugar (about 6 g per small cup, but it adds up over 3-4 cups a day), almost no fibre or protein, and caffeine from the tea. Tea-stall and cafe cups are often larger, use more sugar (2-3 tsp) and sometimes more milk, so the typical restaurant cup scores lower (est.).

researchRating.basis: arguably India's most loved everyday drink, with a very large number of recipe pages, chai-guide articles and cutting-chai write-ups, all describing the same ginger-cardamom-milk-tea base. Points off because the exact spice mix and strength are a matter of personal taste, so recipes differ a lot. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform ratings were not used.

storage: Best fresh. If you must keep it, cool it, strain it and refrigerate in a closed container for up to 1 day (milk tea; not source-checked); reheat in a pan until just steaming (do not boil again) or microwave in 20 second bursts, stirring in between. Freezing is not recommended.
leftoverRemix: Chai-spiced porridge or French toast soak. Use 2-3 tbsp leftover chai in place of milk in a bowl of oats (cook as usual) for a mildly spiced porridge. Leftover chai should have been refrigerated and used the next day (est., not source-checked).
burnOff: about 1.3 km of running (90 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 1.8 km of brisk walking (about 22 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: milk, sugar (or rock sugar), ginger and cardamom are not grains, but strict vrat rule sets avoid tea leaves or caffeine and use sendha-only diets; in those homes swap the tea for plain spiced milk or herbal tea (assumption: the common rule set; families differ; not source-checked this run)

ekadashi.reason: no grain is used, but some households avoid tea on Ekadashi; use spiced milk without tea leaves if so (not source-checked this run; families differ)

jain.reason: swap fresh ginger for dry ginger powder (sonth) 0.3 g; no onion, garlic, roots, meat, egg or honey otherwise

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a light, warm drink that suits iftar, but tea is a mild diuretic, so at sehri keep to one cup with water alongside (not source-checked this run)

jain.reason: fresh ginger is a root (Patch 05 rule); replace the 3 g fresh ginger with 0.3 g dry ginger powder (sonth); everything else (milk, tea, sugar, cardamom) is allowed

vegan.reason: the main recipe uses cow milk (100 ml); use soy or oat milk (see Vegan variant)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: the recipe has no onion or garlic

glutenFree.reason: tea, milk, sugar, ginger and cardamom; no wheat, rava, maida or hing

dairyFree.reason: milk; use plant milk (see Dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: Main recipe already gluten-free (no wheat, rava, maida or hing).
